A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISM research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures and prompts, support reliable comparison. Relocated and renamed material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on NSD, BOLD5000 and GOD, image-question-answering results, alignment measurements and ablation studies, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline results, voxel-gradient analysis, keyword-initialization robustness results and qualitative object-count comparisons.

M1.justification: The structured-text representation, encoder training, keyword-search algorithm and object-centric diffusion procedure remain unchanged. Equations (1)–(7) and Algorithm 1 are retained. The newly documented negative prompt does not establish that the underlying procedure changed between versions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate reconstruction on NSD, BOLD5000 and GOD and question answering on reconstructed NSD images. The additional analyses use retained coverage; keyword initialization is an experimental setting, and two-versus-four-object configurations were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds MindBridge and NeuralDiffuser to reconstruction comparisons on all three datasets, substantially extending the evaluated comparator set with cross-subject and visual-feature-guided approaches. Existing baselines and SDXL comparisons remain. The question-answering comparator set in Table 3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols compute test-set token-to-voxel gradients and aggregate them by brain region (Section 4.4), and exclude spatial keywords from search initialization (Appendix J). Existing dataset splits, reconstruction metrics, training schedules and generative backbones are retained. Correcting 'three metrics' to 'five' describes metrics already used in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantive neural interpretability analysis, tests whether keyword search recovers spatial terms without spatial initialization, and supplies qualitative grouping and omission comparisons for the existing two/four-object variants (Figures 5–6). The earlier latent-space, component and object-count ablations remain, including relocated appendix material.

E5.justification: Both versions describe five-run, across-subject reporting with standard deviations for the main comparisons. Added baseline rows follow that practice. No changed run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Retained table entries are unchanged, but Table 2 adds results for two baselines across three datasets; their NSD LPIPS values are 0.6977 for MindBridge and 0.6522 for NeuralDiffuser. New findings include PreS/VMV1 mean voxel intensities of 0.0080/0.0028, spatial-keyword recovery in Table 9, and object-omission examples. The prose improvement estimate changes to 6%, without a corresponding change in PRISM's tabulated performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, alignment formulas, optimization objective, training loss and diffusion equations are retained, including Appendix B. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced; the gradient-based analysis is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion reduce the claimed maximum perceptual-loss improvement from 8% to 6%; Section 4.2 changes its separate 17% statement to 6%. The central claims about language-space alignment, structured text and object-centric reconstruction remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds a tentative brain-region explanation for spatial-keyword alignment and explicitly acknowledges the need for neuroscience validation. Appendix H replaces v1's human attention/memory-capacity rationale for two objects with an explanation involving grouped descriptions and diffusion-related object omission, supported by qualitative examples.

D1.justification: v2 documents shared negative-prompt use, describes Stable Diffusion 2.1 adaptations for the added baselines, and supplies a code-availability link in the abstract. Existing hardware, hyperparameters and prompt templates remain. Section 8 nevertheless retains the earlier promise of a future code release, leaving the availability wording inconsistent.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially expands its discussion to include BraVL, MindDiffuser, cross-subject approaches such as MindTuner and Wills Aligner, and video reconstruction through NeuroClips and BrainNEDS. New baseline and neuroscience references are added, while the memory-capacity references supporting the former two-object explanation are removed.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, updates author ordering and publication headers, rewrites portions of the explanations and related work, and reorganizes the appendices into separately named sections. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact; the revision is not a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with object-generation diagrams in Figures 4–6, a new robustness table, and additional comparator rows in Table 2. Parts of Figure 1 are redrawn. The reconstruction montage is retained but resized and relocated, while v1's keyword-score Figure 4 becomes Figure 7 with updated labeling.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons, keyword-initialization test and object-count examples strengthen validation and clarify behavior beyond v1's evidence. The revised object-count explanation is more directly connected to observed reconstructions, and the new neural interpretation includes a validation caveat. These are useful but limited gains: the central method and benchmark scores remain unchanged, the neural account is exploratory, and code-release wording remains inconsistent.
